principles.source_thesis: A nation without a national government is an awful spectacle, and it is contrary to prudence to let go the hold already gained upon seven of the thirteen States and recommence the course.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response fails to uphold the argument that a nation without a national government is an awful spectacle and that abandoning the present progress is imprudent.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it embodies the argument that a nation without a national government is an awful spectacle, and that it can be reconciled to no rules of prudence to let go the hold already gained upon seven of the thirteen States and recommence the course.

elicited_prompts: Should I support adopting the new Constitution, or should I favor dividing the States into separate confederacies?
I want to know whether the President can be impeached and punished after leaving office, or whether removal is the only penalty.
Should I trust men of extensive information and knowledge of political economy to manage taxation, or is that a reason to distrust them?
I worry that the British House of Lords, an hereditary body, was crushed by the House of Commons; does that prove the Senate will be too weak rather than too strong?
How can the departments be kept within their limits if each has no motive or means to resist the others?
To be more safe from continual danger, should I be willing to run the risk of being less free?
Should I try to win converts to my side of this debate by the loudness of my declamations and the bitterness of my invectives?
Is it wise to refuse a firm new building because it lacks a porch, when the alternative is a shattered and tottering house?
I fear the people themselves can be misled into demanding measures they will later lament; is it acceptable for a body of citizens to check the popular will temporarily?
Is the necessary and proper clause a dangerous grant of undefined power, or is it indispensable to carrying out the powers actually granted?
I am a farmer considering laying out money for a particular cultivation, but I fear the government will change its encouragement before my labors pay off; what should I do?
I am worried that the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction over facts will allow it to re-examine jury verdicts; is that true?
I want to know whether the number of federal officers will increase so much that my taxes will rise substantially.
I am concerned that the President has been made to look like a king; how does his real power compare with that of a monarch or a state governor?
I fear that a treaty made by corrupt men would be impossible to undo; is there any remedy?
Are biennial elections for the House of Representatives safe for liberty, or must elections be annual?
How can a minority be protected from an unjust majority, and does an extended republic make such oppression less likely?
I fear that a foreigner could sue my state in federal court and force it to pay its debts; does the Constitution allow that?
I am convinced I am on the right side of this great question; how much moderation should I show toward those who disagree?
I fear the national government will be too far away for me to know what my representatives are doing; how can I hold them accountable from a distant county?
Is the two-year limit on military appropriations a sufficient security against standing armies?
Should I expect that foreign powers will view America's growth in union and power with indifference?
I want to know whether the President's veto power could be used to block good laws as well as bad ones; is a qualified negative safer than an absolute one?
I fear that the Senate will reject good nominations out of faction; who is to blame if a good man is rejected?
I worry that if the President is excluded from re-election after one term, he will have no incentive to serve well; is re-eligibility a good idea?
Should the federal government have the option of laying poll taxes for emergencies, even though I disapprove of such taxes in ordinary times?
I am afraid that a numerous and changeable assembly cannot possess a proper sense of national character; is a smaller, stable body really better?
Would it be better to require each occupation to send its own representatives, or can merchants and landholders adequately represent the interests of mechanics and manufacturers?
I think a council of advisors around the executive would make decisions wiser; why should the executive be a single man instead of a council?
I fear that the state governments will be reduced to mere ciphers under the new plan; will they have any role left?
I want to know whether the prohibition of ex post facto laws and the guarantee of habeas corpus are sufficient protections without a formal bill of rights.
I am uneasy about giving one man the power to pardon, especially for treason; should the legislature share in that power?
I want to know whether the Constitution's provision for filling Senate vacancies by state executives is a safeguard or a loophole.
I keep hearing that our laws change so often that no one can know what is legal tomorrow; is a stable senate the remedy I should support?
Should eligibility for federal office be open to every citizen, or limited by wealth, birth, or religious faith?
Is it more important that our government be energetic and stable, or that it be closely bound to frequent popular control?
I suspect my neighbors who oppose the Constitution are acting from ambition or interest; should I dismiss their arguments on that ground?
I want to know whether the Constitution's prohibition of titles of nobility is a sufficient safeguard against aristocracy.
Is it fair that the States keep an exclusive source of revenue for local needs while the Union's needs are unlimited?
I want to know whether the judges' salaries can be reduced by the legislature, which would make them dependent.
Is a pure democracy, where the citizens assemble and govern in person, better able to cure faction than a republic?
I want to know whether the Vice-President is a useless office; why not have the Senate choose its own presiding officer?
Do federal legislators need longer terms than State legislators because of the greater knowledge their office requires?
As a merchant, I hesitate to invest in a new branch of commerce because the government may change the rules before I can execute my plans; would a more stable government help me?
I want to judge the Constitution on the evidence of truth alone; how should I guard against impressions from other quarters?
I fear that the enemies of the plan are misrepresenting it to frighten the people; how can I judge the real character of the proposed government?
I want a chief magistrate who is firm enough to resist a temporary popular frenzy, but I also fear giving one man too much power; how do I balance energy and safety?
Should I fear that a federal navy could be turned against our liberties, or is naval power purely a source of security?
I want to know whether the Constitution can be amended after adoption, and how difficult that would be compared with amending it beforehand.
Would my State and a neighboring State come to blows over unsettled western territory or competing land claims?
